records.name: Pasión y Arte Flamenco
records.summary: A Philadelphia flamenco dance company that teaches classes and stages shows, festivals and tablao nights. Its fall and winter classes are listed on its own site.
records.what_you_do: Take flamenco classes, or go to a performance or festival listed on the company's calendar.

schedule.text: Classes run in fall and winter sessions. The day and time grid is posted as an image on the Classes page, so check there for current times.

cost.text: Drop-in classes are $18 each, or $96 for a card of six classes.

first_step.how: Sign up for a drop-in class or a card of six through the Zeffy sign-up link on the Classes page.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to the public at listed drop-in prices with a clear sign-up link, but the page does not say that beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Elba Hevia y Vaca, the company's artistic and executive director, teaches the classes at the studio on Overbrook Avenue. Every level covers the same core areas: posture and placement, footwork, and music, including rhythm and clapping. A drop-in class is $18, or $96 for a card of six, and students and dance professionals can ask about a discount.
first_visit_tips: Check the Classes page for the current day and time grid before you come.
Email info@pasionyarteflamenco.org if you are unsure which level suits you.
Students and dance professionals can ask about a discount when you sign up.

records.notes: The Fall/Winter 2026 day and time grid is a posted image that could not be read, so no days or times are recorded. The printed year is 2026 (heading and schedule link), but no month is printed, so last_sign_of_life is left out and status rests on the 2026 schedule. The Flamenco Tablao on Saturday, October 10 at Teatro Esperanza prints no year and was not used as dated evidence. A search result (Temple News, not used as a source) describes the studio as a garage behind the founder's home. The listed address is the company's own published address, so the owner may want to decide whether it should show. The old menu item Sevillana Get Togethers 2020 is not used. Whether beginners are welcome is not stated on the pages read.

records.name: Patchwork: A Storytelling Guild
records.summary: A storytelling guild that puts on public story nights and showcases, with free or pay-what-you-can tickets, at venues that include The Rotunda on Walnut Street.
records.what_you_do: Come to a story night as an audience member, or apply to tell a story at a showcase. Story swaps need registration through the site's links.

schedule.text: Story nights and showcases several times a year, mostly at The Rotunda on Walnut Street, with others at the Chestnut Hill Library and the Ice House in Bethlehem, and some held online.

cost.text: Most shows are free or pay what you can, and some suggest $15 a person.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for a story night through the ticket link on the events page. To tell a story, use the teller application or open call when one is listed.
first_step.basis: Public shows are open to anyone with a ticket link, and teller calls are listed separately, but the page does not say how beginners are helped to tell a story.
first_step.what_to_expect: A story night is a live show: a host introduces several tellers, and each one tells a story aloud while the audience listens. Showcases usually run about an hour to two hours, and some shows add an open mic. Most shows are free or pay what you can, and some suggest $15.
first_visit_tips: Buy your ticket ahead through the link on the events page, since many shows need one.
Many shows are pay what you can, so bring what fits your budget.
Start times vary from early afternoon to 7 pm, so check the event page for yours.

records.notes: The Ice House show is printed as Saturday, October 24 with no year. October 24 is a Saturday in 2026, but the year is not printed, so the tier 1 year was not carried over and last_sign_of_life uses the newest year-stated item, Tellabration 2025 (November 2025). Partner names seen on the events page with no URL captured: Friends of Chestnut Hill Library (runs a ghost walk at the library) and ProjectHOME (receives show donations). Online events are listed on the events page, but their current dates were not confirmed, so online_ok comes from the listed Zoom events. Teller application deadlines on the page are old and were not used.

records.name: Penn AC Rowing Association
records.summary: The rowing section of Penn Athletic Club. It runs open learn-to-row classes, junior rowing tracks, a summer camp for high school students, adult masters rowing, and a high performance group.
records.what_you_do: Take a learn-to-row class, then move on to a junior, masters, or high performance track.

schedule.text: Learn to Row runs in four sessions from spring into early fall, with a weeknight class and a Saturday class each week.

cost.text: Learn to Row costs $350 per level.

first_step.how: Register for a Learn to Row level on RegattaCentral (a free account is needed) before the level starts. Walk-ins are not accepted, and questions go to ltr@pennac.org.
first_step.basis: The Learn to Row page is written for adults with no rowing experience and explains how to register online, though it does not take walk-ins.
first_step.what_to_expect: Learn to Row is for adults aged 21 and older with no rowing experience. Each level meets for 90 minutes twice a week, one weeknight and one Saturday, over several weeks, and you finish level 1 before level 2. If a class does not fill it may be moved, and a canceled class is refunded in full.
first_visit_tips: Register early: applications close the day before each level starts, and walk-ins are not accepted.
The page does not list what to wear or bring, so email ltr@pennac.org before your first class.
Start with level 1, since the levels must be taken in order.

records.notes: Canonical record for three pennac.org entries. penn-athletic-club and penn-athletic-club-rowing are marked duplicate and point here. Learn to Row is for ages 21 and up. The junior programs (Junior Learn to Row, Junior Development Program, High Performance Junior, Penn AC Gold summer camp) and the masters and high performance programs are pages on the same site and were not checked in depth, so they are not separate records. Last sign of life is the 2026 session starting August 15, the newest dated item on the program page. The site says membership is open to all experience levels and links a membership application, which was not opened. No street address for the boathouse was found on the pages read.

records.name: Penn Museum
records.summary: A museum in University City. Its Cartifacts volunteers set up carts of five to ten artifacts in the galleries and talk with visitors about each object's history and use.
records.what_you_do: Set up themed carts of artifacts in the galleries, then explain each object to visitors of all ages. Each cart is tied to a gallery, and volunteers pick the subject they want to learn.

schedule.text: Volunteer shifts run Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm. Each volunteer commits to at least four hours a month, and weekend volunteers are especially needed.

access.notes: Ramps or power-assisted doors at the Main and East entrances, borrowable manual wheelchairs, and accessible restrooms on the Lower Level. The third floor Etruscan Italy and Greece galleries are reached by stairs, and staff can point you to a lift. The museum page says it is near SEPTA Penn Medicine Station, and the line is not named.

first_step.how: Submit the online Apply Now form for the Cartifacts volunteer role, or email volunteer@pennmuseum.org with questions.
first_step.basis: Volunteers must apply for a listed role, applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the page describes no beginner training.
first_step.what_to_expect: You set up a cart of five to ten objects that share a theme tied to one gallery, then talk with visitors of all ages about each object. Shifts run Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm. The page does not describe training, so ask what a first shift looks like before you commit.
first_visit_tips: Apply first, since the museum reviews applications on a rolling basis.
Parking may be tight: the museum garage on Convention Avenue is under renovation, with Penn Park Garage and Chestnut 34 Garage as backups.
Weekend volunteers are especially needed, so say if you can do weekends.

records.notes: Cartifacts is the only listed volunteer role on the jobs page. The Plan Your Visit page prints ZIP 19014 for the museum, which is a typo, so the footer ZIP 19104 is used. Museum hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 5 pm. The accessibility page gives Visitor Services at 215.898.4001 for questions about sensory and ASL services, which it does not cover. No background check, clearance or letter is mentioned for volunteers. The jobs page does not name a minimum age, only mature high school students and adults.

records.name: Pennsport String Band
records.summary: A Mummers string band in Philadelphia that plays weddings, parades, and festivals. It says it is always looking for new members, and its rehearsals are open to anyone.
records.what_you_do: Play an instrument in the band, or help out as a non-musician. Ask for the next rehearsal time and place, since the site does not publish them.

schedule.text: Rehearsals are open to anyone, but the site does not publish days or times.

locations.label: Address listed on the band's site

cost.text: Dues and costs are not published.

first_step.how: Email pennsportstringband@gmail.com or use the Contact Us link on the band's site to ask about the next rehearsal.
first_step.basis: The home page says rehearsals are open to beginners and seasoned players, that non-musicians are welcome to help, and it points people to its contact page to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first rehearsal. Players range from beginners to experienced musicians, and non-musicians are welcome to pitch in. Rehearsal times, the place, and any costs are not published, so ask about them when you get in touch.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the rehearsal time and place before you go, since the site does not list them.
You do not need an instrument to help out as a non-musician.

records.notes: The site is thin: the home page is the only page that loaded. pennsportstringband.com/contact-us/, /contact/ and /members/ all returned 404. The 38 Jackson Street address is the band's published contact address. The site does not say it is a rehearsal space, and it may be a private home, so the owner may want to check before the address shows. The home page names two contacts with personal phone numbers. Those were not recorded, and the general band email is used. Status is probably_active because the site works but shows no dated activity; its only dates are history (formed 2007, parade 2008).
